subtopics.content: Definition, functions, sections, departments, office personnel, professional image, layout
subtopics.objective: Understand office functions (receiving, recording, processing, storing information, protecting assets); identify roles of reception, stores, mail room; detail department interrelationships (Accounts, Sales, HR, Legal, Transport); differentiate roles of office staff (Manager, Supervisor, Clerks, Secretaries, Typist); examine personal/business attributes, time management, and open vs closed office layouts.

Apply organization principles (span of control, unity of command, delegation, authority/responsibility); evaluate organizational structures (Line, Line and staff, Functional, Matrix); draw and interpret organograms.

subtopics.content: Transaction documents, payment methods, payroll, tax, petty cash, bank account types, cheques
subtopics.objective: Identify and complete business documents (LPO, Invoice, Debit/Credit Notes, Waybill, Statement of Account); explain payment methods; compute payroll (gross/net pay, PAYE, piece/time rates); understand tax regimes (VAT, Income, Customs Duty); operate imprest petty cash system; distinguish commercial/central bank functions, savings/current/fixed accounts, and cheque features/crossings.

topics.title: Stock Procedure, Office Equipment, and Machines

subtopics.content: Stock ordering, storekeeper duties, stock records, valuation, general/computer/mailroom machines
subtopics.objective: Describe stock ordering, storekeeper duties, requisitioning, and stock control levels (minimum, maximum, re-order); compare stock valuation methods; evaluate factors in purchasing office equipment; operate computers, photocopiers, risographs, calculators, fax machines, franking/shredding machines, and mailroom equipment.

subtopics.content: Communication forms/barriers, business correspondence, mail handling, meetings, proofreading, filing
subtopics.objective: Identify oral/written/visual communication forms and barriers; draft business letters, memos, and report types; manage incoming/outgoing mail registers; plan meetings, understand terminologies (quorum, agenda, motion), draft minutes; apply proofreading, spelling, and punctuation rules; classify filing systems (alphabetical, numerical, subject) and indexing.

topics.title: Reference Books, Post Office, Human Relations, Health, Pre-Employment, and Entrepreneurship

subtopics.content: Sources of info, postal/courier services, interpersonal skills, office safety/welfare, recruitment, small business
subtopics.objective: Utilize general/specialized reference books and official documents (passports, visas); understand postal, express, and courier services; apply human relations and public relations skills; identify office health hazards, accident prevention, and staff welfare; prepare job advertisements, application letters, CVs, and interview skills; understand characteristics and importance of small-scale business entrepreneurship.
